The samples should now be checked for successful amplification, contamination in negatives and any secondary banding. Gel electrophoresis will achieve this, but digital systems like the Qiagen Qiaxcel will do this and facilitate equalisation by generating amplicon-specific DNA concentrations (see the robotics-based protocol step-case).

Equalisation is more effective than normalisation, but requires amplicon concentration data. Both can be time and labour intensive though, so can be skipped if time restricted for large-scale projects, although at the expense of data recovery and evenness. The robotics-based protocol step-case goes through equalisation using a Qiagen Qiaxcel, but this process could also be emulated by bead-cleaning all of the samples individually (as per the bead clean in the equalisation protocol following the pooling steps), and then using a Qubit fluorometer (or similar) to quantify the concentrations of amplicons. Samples could then be pooled based on Qubit concentrations, and will then be ready for library preparation (no further bead cleaning necessary unless the overall concentration is low and you would like to concentrate the library by eluting into a smaller volume). If doing that, it is crucial that the Qubit measurements are taken after bead cleaning so that primers and primer dimers do not contribute to the DNA concentrations used for pooling. If the PCRs were replicated (i.e., each sample run multiple times for each PCR primer pair used), these can be merged together into one plate at this point, or carried forward separately. Keeping the replicates separate increases the number of libraries to prepare and sequence later, but better facilitates inconsistencies between samples. To merge triplicates, assuming use of 10 µL reaction volumes, pipette 8 µL from each well of two of the three plates into the corresponding well of the third. Briefly centrifuge the merged plate to move the oil to the top of the product again. To avoid pipetting oil from the oil-sealed PCR products, plunge the pipette to the first stop and fully insert the pipette tip into the bottom of the well, then release sharply. The PCR product will be taken up quickly, whereas the relatively viscous oil will be taken up slowly, thus being outcompeted by the PCR product.

steps.title: Sample Preparation and Dissection
steps.instruction: Prepare samples for molecular analysis by removing non-target tissue and transferring them to a 96-well plate.

substeps.instruction: Use sterilised forceps and a sterile scalpel/ethanol to clear away non-target tissue (e.g., non-gut tissue).
Decontaminate tools and surfaces (e.g., Petri dish) between samples with Chemgene, rinse with molecular biology-grade water and 100% ethanol, and wipe dry with sterile tissue.
Transfer individual samples into 96-well plates (ideally 2.2 mL deep-well with fixable lids).
Store samples at -20 °C until processing. If defrosting, warm the plate to 50-60 °C if TNES precipitates.

steps.title: Sample Homogenisation
steps.instruction: Homogenise the samples using a tissue grinder and carbon steel beads.

substeps.instruction: Add one 3 mm hardened carbon steel bead to each well (beads must be baked at 250 °C for at least 12 hours to remove manufacturing oil).
Centrifuge the plate at 2000 x g at room temperature for 2 minutes.
Add 100 µL TNES lysis buffer (100 mM Tris-HCl, 52 mM NaCl, 10 mM EDTA, 10% volume SDS) to each well.
Grind samples in a tissue grinder/homogeniser at 1750 rpm at room temperature for 1 minute.

steps.title: Lysis and Protein Inactivation
steps.instruction: Lyse the samples and inactivate proteins using Proteinase K and Lysis Buffer 2.

substeps.instruction: Grind larvae in a Geno/Grinder 2010 at full speed (1750 RPM) for 4 minutes; repeat if not fully homogenised.
Centrifuge at 4,000 g for 2 minutes.
Remove ball bearings using a magnet.
Add 1 mL of Proteinase Buffer master mix (Lysis Buffer 2 [pH 9: 120 mM NaCl, 50 mM 1 M Tris-Hcl, 20 mM 0.5 M EDTA, 3% SDS, H2O] and Proteinase K [10 mg/mL]) to the lysate and vortex.
Incubate at 37 °C overnight (12-16 hours).
Centrifuge at 4000 x g for 4 minutes.
Transfer 1 mL of supernatant to a clean 2.2 mL deep-well 96-well plate for backup; retain the rest in the original plate.
Centrifuge at 2000 x g for 4 minutes.
Transfer 200 μL of the supernatant to a clean 2.2 mL deep-well 96-well plate; store remaining lysate at -20 °C.

steps.title: DNA Extraction via Magnetic Beads
steps.instruction: Extract DNA using the BOMB-Bio magnetic bead method.

substeps.instruction: To a 96-well deep-well plate, add 60 µL lysate, 120 µL 1.5X GITC buffer (6 M GITC, 75 mM Tris-HCl, 3% sarkosyl, 30 mM EDTA, 0.15% antifoam), 120 µL 1 mg/mL SeraMag Speed Beads in TE (10 mM Tris, 1 mM EDTA), and 240 µL isopropanol.
Mix by pipetting or vortexing (1500 rpm, room temperature, 1 minute).
Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Place on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes.
Remove all but 5 µL of the mixture via pipette.
Add 400 µL 80% volume ethanol to each well.
Remove ethanol entirely and discard.
Remove ethanol as completely as possible and air-dry beads until they transition from 'glossy' to 'matte' (avoid rusty red/cracks).
Add 105 µL molecular grade water, shake at 1500 rpm (room temperature, 1 minute), and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Place on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes.
Remove 100 µL of the supernatant for PCR.
Store eluted DNA at -20 °C.

steps.title: PCR Amplification
steps.instruction: Perform PCR using tagged primers and a thermocycler.

substeps.instruction: Prepare PCR mastermix for 25 µL reaction volumes.
Create a primer plate with both PCR primers at 5 µM concentration (using 8 uniquely tagged forward and 12 uniquely tagged reverse primers).
Add 22.75 µL hot-start Taq polymerase and water master mix to each well, followed by 1.25 µL of primer mix.
Add 1 µL DNA to sample/positive control wells and 1 µL molecular grade water to negative controls.
Distribute one drop (~20 µL) of mineral oil into each well.
Briefly centrifuge the plate to ensure oil is above the mix and no bubbles exist.
Load into thermocycler and run the program matching the enzyme and primer annealing temperatures.

steps.title: PCR Product Purification and Equalisation
steps.instruction: Purify PCR products and pool them to achieve equimolarity.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 0.1X SPRI bead solution: Mix 5 mL 1X bead solution with 45 mL of a mix containing 25 mL 5 M NaCl, 3.582 mL water, 0.168 mL 1 N HCl, 0.5 mL 1 M Tris base, 0.5 mL 0.1 M disodium EDTA, and 20 mL 50% PEG.
Add 20 µL of 0.1X SPRI bead solution (or volume equivalent to available PCR product) to a new 96-well plate.
Add 20 µL PCR product (avoiding oil) and vortex (1500 rpm, room temperature, 1 minute).
Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes, then place on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes.
Remove all but 5 µL of the mixture.
Add 200 µL 80% ethanol, then repeat adding another 200 µL 80% ethanol.
Remove ethanol and place on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes.
Add 10 µL molecular grade water, shake at 1500 rpm (room temperature, 1 minute), and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Pool 8 µL from each well into a single tube (calculate volumes based on amplicon concentration to achieve equimolarity).
Mix pooled samples by flicking/inverting and transfer 700 µL to a 2.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.

steps.title: Final Library Purification
steps.instruction: Perform final purification of the pooled library using 1X magnetic beads.

substeps.instruction: Add 700 µL 1X magnetic beads to the pooled sample and vortex; incubate for 5 minutes.
Place on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes.
Add 400 µL 80% ethanol, then repeat adding another 400 µL 80% ethanol.
Remove ethanol completely, centrifuge briefly, and air-dry beads until 'matte'.
Add 100 µL molecular grade water, vortex, and incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Place on a magnetic stand for 5 minutes.
Remove 95 µL of the water as the final library.

steps.title: Quantification and Sequencing
steps.instruction: Quantify the final library and prepare for sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Quantify library concentration (e.g., using Qubit dsDNA assay).
Follow manufacturer protocols for Oxford Nanopore or Illumina sequencing based on primer overhangs and provider requirements.
